# Judith Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_006_page_001.jpg

---

**6:1** When the uproar around the war council died down, Holofernes — supreme commander of the Assyrian forces — turned to Achior and the Moabites before the whole assembly of his allied peoples:

**6:2** "Just who do you think you are, Achior? You and your Ephraimite hirelings come here prophesying that we should not fight Israel because their god will protect them? What god is there but Nebuchadnezzar? He will unleash his power and sweep them off the face of the earth — their god cannot save them.

**6:3** We are his servants and we will cut them down like one man. No force of theirs can stand against our cavalry.

**6:4** We will swallow them whole. Their mountains will run drunk with their blood and their plains will be carpeted with their dead. Their footsteps will vanish before us — they will be annihilated. This is the word of King Nebuchadnezzar, master of all the earth. He has spoken it, and what he speaks does not go unfulfilled.

**6:5** As for you, Achior — you mercenary hired out to Ammon — you spoke these words today in your folly. From this day forward you will not look upon my face again, not until I exact my vengeance on this people who crawled out of Egypt.

**6:6** Then the iron of my soldiers and the spears of my forces will go through your ribs, and you will lie among their dead when I come back.

**6:7** For now, my men will drag you up into the highlands and dump you in one of the mountain villages.

**6:8** You will not die until you die with them.

**6:9** If your heart is so set on believing they will escape capture — fine. Do not look so stricken. I have spoken. Every word I have spoken will come true."

**6:10** Holofernes ordered the guards standing at ready in his tent to arrest Achior, haul him to Bethulia, and deliver him into the hands of the Israelites.

**6:11** The guards grabbed him and marched him out of the camp, across the plain, and up into the hill country until they reached the springs below Bethulia.

**6:12** The men of the city spotted them on the ridge, snatched up their weapons, and charged out to the hilltop. Every slinger in the city pelted them with rocks, pinning them down and blocking their ascent.

**6:13** The soldiers ducked below the ridge, trussed Achior up, and left him lying at the foot of the hill before heading back to Holofernes.

**6:14** The Israelites came down from the city, found him, cut him free, brought him into Bethulia, and set him before the city leaders.

**6:15** The leaders at that time were Uzziah son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon; Chabris son of Gothoniel; and Charmis son of Melchiel.

**6:16** They summoned every elder in the city. All the young men crowded in, and the women too. They placed Achior in the center of the whole assembly, and Uzziah questioned him about everything that had happened.

**6:17** He told them everything — the proceedings of Holofernes' council, what the Assyrian commanders had said, and every arrogant boast Holofernes had made against the house of Israel.

**6:18** The people threw themselves to the ground and worshiped God, crying out:

**6:19** "O Lord, God of heaven — look at their arrogance! Have pity on our people in our misery. Look today with favor on those who belong to you."

**6:20** Then they rallied Achior and praised him warmly.

**6:21** Uzziah brought him from the assembly to his own house and held a feast for the elders. They spent the whole night calling on the God of Israel for help.
